summary: Service token bound to stale SAML session prevents newly-provisioned service roles from propagating to internal tooling
description:
Issue summary: Several internal service accounts suddenly lost elevated runtime permissions after an admin granted new roles in Okta. The affected service tokens continued to authorize against the console but lacked newly-granted delegated scopes, causing runbook automation and service impersonation to fail.

Impact: Multiple internal automation tasks that rely on service account impersonation (runbook executions, nightly model-eval triggers, and support tooling) returned 403s. No customer-facing API impact reported, but internal on-call workflows were blocked for ~2 hours.

Observed behavior: When a role is added to a service account in Okta (via SCIM), the console and service-provisioner accept the change in the user record, but long-lived service tokens issued prior to the role-change do not pick up the new scopes. Tokens remain valid for auth but are missing the delegated 'impersonate:runbook' and 'admin:trigger-eval' scopes.

Expected behavior: After role change and SCIM sync, existing service tokens should either be invalidated or their effective authorization claims should refresh so newly-granted roles are honored immediately or within the configured TTL.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create or use an existing long-lived service account token (issued before role changes).
2) In Okta, add an elevated role to the service account (e.g., 'runbook-executor') and let SCIM sync complete.
3) Call internal impersonation endpoint with the pre-existing token to trigger a runbook.
4) Observe 403 with 'missing scope' error in runbook logs while Okta UI shows the role attached.
5) Force a token rotation and observe runbook succeeds immediately.
logs:
Relevant log excerpts (sanitized):
- auth-proxy: WARN token-claims-miss match=service-account-42 expected_scopes=[impersonate:runbook,admin:trigger-eval] found_scopes=[read:model,write:logs] ts=2026-03-12T08:14:05Z
- service-provisioner: INFO scim-sync user=svc-runner-42 status=updated attrs_changed=[roles] ts=2026-03-12T08:12:50Z
- console-auth: DEBUG session-lookup token=**** old_saml_id=adfs|SAML1234 last_checked=2026-03-12T07:05:01Z
- runbook-engine: ERROR impersonation_denied user=svc-runner-42 reason="missing_scope:impersonate:runbook" request_id=abc-123 ts=2026-03-12T08:14:07Z
investigation_notes:
Timeline: SCIM sync completed at 08:12:50Z, errors from runbook engine started at 08:14Z. Hypothesis: identity-proxy caches a token->session mapping and derives active scopes from the SAML assertion that was present at token issuance. When Okta roles change via SCIM, the user record updates but cached session metadata (bound to original SAML assertion KID/ID) is not invalidated.

Evidence: - trace from auth-proxy shows token tied to old_saml_id. - No SCIM failure logged; changes reached service-provisioner successfully. - Forcing token rotation (reissue) immediately resolved the 403s.

Temporary mitigations attempted: - Forced cache eviction for impacted token keys in auth-proxy (manual). This restored access for 3 of 4 affected service accounts. - Notified owners to rotate long-lived tokens as stop-gap.

Root-cause theory: Caching layer in identity-proxy attaches a token->session snapshot at first validation. That snapshot included the original assertion claims. When SCIM updates roles, the snapshot is stale. There is no mechanism to detect role-change events and invalidate affected snapshots nor does the service-provisioner broadcast token invalidation for service tokens.

Related traces/dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/identity/token-claims?from=2026-03-12T07:00:00Z&to=2026-03-12T09:00:00Z
Slack incident channel: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C09SUPPORT/2357
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Initial report received from oncall; runbook failures started at 08:14Z. Investigating whether SCIM successfully updated roles. Assigned to Ravi for oncall triage.

Ravi Patel (Oncall): Confirmed SCIM update present in service-provisioner logs. Observed token claims mismatch in auth-proxy. Forced cache eviction for token keys for three svc accounts; one account needed manual token rotation. Opening follow-up with infra team.

Ava Morgan (Identity Eng): Looked at identity-proxy code paths — caching TTL is 24h and eviction only occurs on explicit logout or token rotation. Proposal: add a role-change hook in service-provisioner to publish token-invalidation events. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/274
Ravi Patel (Oncall): Temporary workaround posted to #oncall-runbooks: rotate long-lived tokens after role changes. Will monitor for recurrence.
resolution: Mitigation: Evicted stale token caches and instructed service owners to rotate long-lived tokens when roles change. Permanent fix: identity-provisioner PR will emit a 'role-change' event to the auth-proxy topic; identity-proxy will listen and invalidate cached token snapshots when relevant user/service account roles change. Planned rollout: PRs merged -> canary deploy to prod-us-east on 2026-03-16 -> global rollout 2026-03-18. Post-incident follow-up: audit long-lived tokens and implement a signal-based token invalidation runbook.
